paths.learner_scope: Beginner-to-job-ready Product Manager (APM/junior-PM level). Assumes general professional communication and basic business literacy. Does not require or re-teach Business Analyst depth (detailed requirements-elicitation technique) or engineering implementation (writing/shipping code). Also does not re-teach SQL/statistical-modeling depth; metrics/analytics content is taught natively at PM-appropriate depth (reading dashboards, interpreting A/B tests) rather than delegated as a cross-path prerequisite.

toc_location.tile_summary: Use a company's mission and values as a constant decision filter, then articulate the product's own aspirational vision statement as a fixed north star distinct from the roadmap.

concepts.primary_objective: Understand a company's mission and values well enough to filter product decisions against them.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a mission/values statement and a proposed feature, judge whether the feature is consistent with them.
concepts.practice_objective: Evaluate two sample feature ideas against a given mission statement and flag any conflict.
concepts.central_mental_model: Mission/values as a constant filter that decisions pass through, sitting above and more stable than any single vision or strategy.

toc_location.tile_summary: Use a company's mission and values as a constant decision filter, then articulate the product's own aspirational vision statement as a fixed north star distinct from the roadmap.

concepts.primary_objective: Articulate a concise, aspirational statement of the future state the product aims to create for its customers and business.
concepts.assessment_target: Given product/company context, write or critique a vision statement for clarity, aspiration, and alignment with strategy.
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a one-sentence product vision statement for a sample product and justify each word choice.
concepts.central_mental_model: Vision as a fixed 'north star' destination, distinct from the roadmap that describes how to get there.

toc_location.tile_title: Value Proposition, Competitive Position & Business Goals
toc_location.tile_summary: Articulate the specific value a product delivers to a segment, assess competitors to find gaps, claim a distinct position in the customer's mind, and trace every one of those back to a stated business goal.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The job the customer is trying to get done, the pain they currently experience, and the gain they seek -- the JTBD framing used to structure a value proposition.

concepts.primary_objective: Articulate the specific value a product delivers to a defined customer segment.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a customer segment and product, write a value proposition stating the job done, pain relieved, and gain created.
concepts.practice_objective: Write a value proposition for a sample product/segment pair using the pain-relief/gain-creation structure.
concepts.central_mental_model: Value proposition as the fit between what customers need and what the product specifically delivers, distinct from generic positioning.

toc_location.tile_title: Value Proposition, Competitive Position & Business Goals
toc_location.tile_summary: Articulate the specific value a product delivers to a segment, assess competitors to find gaps, claim a distinct position in the customer's mind, and trace every one of those back to a stated business goal.

concepts.primary_objective: Systematically assess competitor products/strategies to identify gaps and threats relevant to a product decision.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of competitors, produce a structured comparison (features, pricing, positioning) and identify one actionable gap.
concepts.practice_objective: Build a comparison table for 3 competitors on a sample dimension set and flag the biggest gap.
concepts.central_mental_model: Competitors as a reference frame for judging a product's relative strengths, not a target to copy feature-for-feature.

toc_location.tile_title: Value Proposition, Competitive Position & Business Goals
toc_location.tile_summary: Articulate the specific value a product delivers to a segment, assess competitors to find gaps, claim a distinct position in the customer's mind, and trace every one of those back to a stated business goal.

concepts.primary_objective: Define where a product sits relative to competitors and alternatives in the customer's mind.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a competitive set, write a positioning statement (for X, who Y, our product is Z, unlike A, we B).
concepts.practice_objective: Complete a positioning statement template for a sample product against two named competitors.
concepts.central_mental_model: Positioning as a claimed spot on a mental map the customer already holds, not a list of features.

toc_location.tile_title: Value Proposition, Competitive Position & Business Goals
toc_location.tile_summary: Articulate the specific value a product delivers to a segment, assess competitors to find gaps, claim a distinct position in the customer's mind, and trace every one of those back to a stated business goal.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A specific, testable belief about what action will produce what result, framed so it can be proven right or wrong.

concepts.primary_objective: Connect a product decision or roadmap item explicitly to a stated business goal.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a business goal and a proposed initiative, trace and justify (or reject) the link between them.
concepts.practice_objective: Map three sample roadmap items to the business goal each one is meant to serve, or flag it as unaligned.
concepts.central_mental_model: Every product bet as a hypothesis about how it moves a specific business number.

toc_location.tile_summary: Conduct one-on-one interviews without leading the witness, reframe what customers say as a job they're hiring a product to do, and cluster raw feedback from support tickets and reviews into recurring themes.

concepts.primary_objective: Plan and conduct one-on-one qualitative interviews to surface unmet customer needs and pain points.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a discovery goal, design and run a customer interview that avoids leading questions and extracts actionable insight.
concepts.practice_objective: Draft an interview guide and conduct a mock customer interview, then identify at least one leading question to fix.
concepts.central_mental_model: An interview as an instrument for surfacing the customer's own words about pain, not for pitching or validating a solution.

toc_location.tile_summary: Conduct one-on-one interviews without leading the witness, reframe what customers say as a job they're hiring a product to do, and cluster raw feedback from support tickets and reviews into recurring themes.

concepts.primary_objective: Apply the Jobs-to-Be-Done framework to reframe a customer problem in terms of the job the customer is 'hiring' a product to do.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a customer scenario, write a JTBD statement (situation, motivation, outcome) instead of a feature request.
concepts.practice_objective: Convert three raw customer feature requests into JTBD statements.
concepts.central_mental_model: A product as something 'hired' to do a job, so the job -- not the demographic -- is the true unit of analysis.

toc_location.tile_summary: Conduct one-on-one interviews without leading the witness, reframe what customers say as a job they're hiring a product to do, and cluster raw feedback from support tickets and reviews into recurring themes.

concepts.primary_objective: Synthesize raw, unstructured customer feedback (support tickets, reviews, calls) into recurring themes.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a batch of raw feedback, cluster it into themes and rank by frequency/severity.
concepts.practice_objective: Tag and cluster a sample set of customer feedback into 3-5 themes.
concepts.central_mental_model: VoC as passive-signal synthesis across many existing feedback channels, distinct from actively solicited interviews.

toc_location.tile_summary: Design survey questions that don't bias the data, divide a market into segments by shared need rather than convenient demographics, and calculate TAM/SAM/SOM to size the opportunity.

concepts.primary_objective: Design a quantitative survey instrument that measures a specific research question without introducing bias.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a research question, write a survey with appropriately-typed questions (avoiding double-barreled/leading items).
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a 5-question survey for a given research question and flag any biased wording.
concepts.central_mental_model: A survey as a precision instrument where question wording directly determines data validity.

toc_location.tile_summary: Design survey questions that don't bias the data, divide a market into segments by shared need rather than convenient demographics, and calculate TAM/SAM/SOM to size the opportunity.

concepts.primary_objective: Divide a market into meaningful segments based on shared needs or characteristics.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a customer dataset/description, propose segments and justify the segmentation variable chosen.
concepts.practice_objective: Segment a sample customer base into 3 groups and describe each segment's defining need.
concepts.central_mental_model: Segmentation as grouping by shared need/behavior, not by convenient demographic buckets.

toc_location.tile_summary: Design survey questions that don't bias the data, divide a market into segments by shared need rather than convenient demographics, and calculate TAM/SAM/SOM to size the opportunity.

concepts.primary_objective: Estimate the total, serviceable, and obtainable market size for a product opportunity.
concepts.assessment_target: Given market inputs, calculate TAM, SAM, and SOM and justify the assumptions behind each.
concepts.practice_objective: Compute TAM/SAM/SOM for a sample opportunity using provided market data.
concepts.central_mental_model: Market size as three nested circles narrowing from total demand to what this product can realistically capture.

toc_location.tile_summary: Turn research into two synthesis-and-validation practices: build a persona from prior interview/survey evidence, and run a usability test to observe real behavior against a prototype.

concepts.primary_objective: Synthesize research findings into a representative customer persona that guides product decisions.
concepts.assessment_target: Given raw research data (interviews, surveys), construct a persona with goals, pain points, and behaviors.
concepts.practice_objective: Build one persona from a sample set of research notes.
concepts.central_mental_model: A persona as a synthesis artifact standing in for a research-backed segment, not a demographic sketch invented from assumption.

toc_location.tile_summary: Turn research into two synthesis-and-validation practices: build a persona from prior interview/survey evidence, and run a usability test to observe real behavior against a prototype.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A pre-release approximation of a product used for testing, ranging in 'fidelity' from a rough low-fidelity sketch/wireframe to a high-fidelity, closely-realistic simulation of the finished product.

concepts.primary_objective: Plan and moderate a usability test session to observe how a user actually completes a task with a design/prototype.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a prototype and a task, write a moderated test script and identify usability breakdowns from a session recording/transcript.
concepts.practice_objective: Run a moderated usability test on a low-fidelity prototype and log at least two usability issues.
concepts.central_mental_model: Usability testing as observing behavior against a task, not asking opinions about a design.

toc_location.tile_summary: Judge whether the product has found genuine product-market fit, synthesizing retention, organic growth, and qualitative signal into one strategic call -- a distinct judgment skill from the research and synthesis techniques that feed it, closing the customer-research phase.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A chart of the percentage of users who remain active over successive time periods after adoption -- used here as supporting evidence for product-market fit, well before retention is taught formally in the metrics_and_analytics family.

concepts.primary_objective: Recognize and evaluate the signals that indicate a product satisfies strong market demand.
concepts.assessment_target: Given usage/retention/qualitative data, judge whether a product has reached product-market fit and cite the evidence.
concepts.practice_objective: Assess a sample dataset (retention curve, survey results) and conclude whether PMF signals are present.
concepts.central_mental_model: PMF as a threshold state evidenced by retention and organic pull, not a permanent achievement.

toc_location.tile_summary: State who is affected and why it matters independent of any fix, reframe the problem to generate multiple candidate directions before committing to one, then specify the chosen solution in enough detail for engineering and design to build against.

concepts.primary_objective: Write a clear, evidence-backed statement of the customer/business problem being addressed.
concepts.assessment_target: Given context/evidence, write a problem statement stating who is affected, what the pain is, and why it matters.
concepts.practice_objective: Write a problem statement for a sample scenario using provided evidence.
concepts.central_mental_model: A problem statement as a claim about pain in the world, testable independent of any proposed fix.

toc_location.tile_summary: State who is affected and why it matters independent of any fix, reframe the problem to generate multiple candidate directions before committing to one, then specify the chosen solution in enough detail for engineering and design to build against.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A five-stage iterative problem-solving sequence -- empathize, define, ideate, prototype, test -- used across product/UX work; this concept teaches the 'ideate' stage specifically, in contrast to sibling concepts covering the others (design_collaboration, design_feedback, user_testing_synthesis, user_journey_mapping).

concepts.primary_objective: Reframe a problem statement and generate a range of candidate solution directions before committing to one, using 'How Might We' framing.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a stated problem, reframe it as a 'How Might We' question and generate 3 distinct candidate solution directions.
concepts.practice_objective: Reframe a sample problem statement and produce 3 candidate directions for it.
concepts.central_mental_model: Ideation widens the solution space deliberately before narrowing, rather than committing to the first plausible idea.

toc_location.tile_summary: State who is affected and why it matters independent of any fix, reframe the problem to generate multiple candidate directions before committing to one, then specify the chosen solution in enough detail for engineering and design to build against.

concepts.primary_objective: Specify a proposed solution's behavior in enough detail for engineering and design to build it.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a problem statement, write a solution specification describing the proposed approach and its boundaries.
concepts.practice_objective: Write a solution specification for a sample approved problem statement.
concepts.central_mental_model: A solution spec as the 'how' that follows and is justified by an already-validated 'why'.

toc_location.tile_summary: Keep a spec's problem framing open to better solutions by separating it from the chosen fix, write the PRD as the artifact of record for both, then compress it into a one-pager a non-specialist can read in under two minutes.

concepts.primary_objective: Keep the problem being solved distinct from the solution chosen to solve it throughout a spec.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a spec draft that conflates problem and solution, identify and separate the two.
concepts.practice_objective: Rewrite a sample muddled requirement into a clean problem statement and a clean solution statement.
concepts.central_mental_model: Problem/solution separation as a discipline that keeps a spec open to better solutions instead of anchoring on the first one.

toc_location.tile_summary: Keep a spec's problem framing open to better solutions by separating it from the chosen fix, write the PRD as the artifact of record for both, then compress it into a one-pager a non-specialist can read in under two minutes.

concepts.primary_objective: Write a PRD that documents what will be built and why, sufficient for engineering to start work.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a feature concept, write a PRD covering problem, solution, and requirements.
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a PRD for a sample feature using the standard sections.
concepts.central_mental_model: PRD as the single artifact of record for a feature's problem and requirements, not a design or implementation spec.

toc_location.tile_summary: Keep a spec's problem framing open to better solutions by separating it from the chosen fix, write the PRD as the artifact of record for both, then compress it into a one-pager a non-specialist can read in under two minutes.

concepts.primary_objective: Summarize an initiative's problem, solution, and impact on a single page for broad audiences.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a PRD or initiative, condense it into a one-pager that a non-specialist can understand in under 2 minutes.
concepts.practice_objective: Write a one-pager summarizing a sample initiative.
concepts.central_mental_model: The one-pager as a compressed, audience-agnostic summary sitting above the detailed PRD.

toc_location.tile_title: User Stories, Acceptance Criteria, User Flows & Success Metrics
toc_location.tile_summary: Write requirements as user stories that hold a placeholder for conversation, define the testable pass/fail conditions each must meet, diagram the steps and branches a user takes to complete a task, and pre-commit to the metrics that will determine if it worked.

concepts.primary_objective: Write user stories in the standard format capturing who, what, and why for a unit of work.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a requirement, write it as a well-formed user story (As a..., I want..., so that...).
concepts.practice_objective: Convert 3 sample requirements into user story format.
concepts.central_mental_model: A user story as a placeholder for a conversation about a specific user need, not a full spec.

toc_location.tile_title: User Stories, Acceptance Criteria, User Flows & Success Metrics
toc_location.tile_summary: Write requirements as user stories that hold a placeholder for conversation, define the testable pass/fail conditions each must meet, diagram the steps and branches a user takes to complete a task, and pre-commit to the metrics that will determine if it worked.

concepts.primary_objective: Define the testable conditions that must be true for a story to be considered done.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a user story, write acceptance criteria that are specific and testable.
concepts.practice_objective: Write acceptance criteria for 2 sample user stories.
concepts.central_mental_model: Acceptance criteria as the pass/fail contract for a story, independent of implementation detail.

toc_location.tile_title: User Stories, Acceptance Criteria, User Flows & Success Metrics
toc_location.tile_summary: Write requirements as user stories that hold a placeholder for conversation, define the testable pass/fail conditions each must meet, diagram the steps and branches a user takes to complete a task, and pre-commit to the metrics that will determine if it worked.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A low-fidelity visual layout showing structure and content placement without final visual design.

concepts.primary_objective: Diagram the sequence of steps a user takes to complete a task within a product.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a task, produce a user flow diagram covering the steps and decision points.
concepts.practice_objective: Sketch a user flow for a sample task with at least one decision branch.
concepts.central_mental_model: A user flow as the map of a task's steps and branches, distinct from a single-screen wireframe.

toc_location.tile_title: User Stories, Acceptance Criteria, User Flows & Success Metrics
toc_location.tile_summary: Write requirements as user stories that hold a placeholder for conversation, define the testable pass/fail conditions each must meet, diagram the steps and branches a user takes to complete a task, and pre-commit to the metrics that will determine if it worked.

concepts.primary_objective: Define the metrics that will determine whether a feature or initiative succeeded.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an initiative's goal, define specific, measurable success metrics and target thresholds.
concepts.practice_objective: Define 2-3 success metrics with target thresholds for a sample feature.
concepts.central_mental_model: Success metrics as the pre-committed measurement of 'did it work,' defined before launch to avoid post-hoc rationalization.

toc_location.tile_summary: Build a roadmap that communicates sequenced bets toward the vision, then calculate the team capacity that constrains how much of it is realistic.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The full set of not-yet-scheduled work items a team maintains; distinct from the roadmap's committed, time-sequenced view.

concepts.primary_objective: Build a roadmap that communicates the sequenced direction of a product over time.
concepts.assessment_target: Given goals and a backlog, construct a roadmap artifact showing sequenced themes over a timeframe.
concepts.practice_objective: Build a one-page roadmap for a sample product spanning two quarters.
concepts.central_mental_model: Roadmap as a living communication artifact showing sequenced bets toward the vision, not a fixed delivery contract.

toc_location.tile_summary: Build a roadmap that communicates sequenced bets toward the vision, then calculate the team capacity that constrains how much of it is realistic.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A team's historical average amount of work (e.g. story points) completed per sprint, used to forecast how much capacity is available for a planning period.
A fixed time-boxed iteration used to plan and estimate near-term delivery work.

An estimation unit representing relative effort/size/complexity (not literal time), assigned to a work item and compared against a reference story on a scale (commonly a Fibonacci-like sequence), used for sizing rather than absolute-hour prediction.

concepts.primary_objective: Estimate how much roadmap work a team can realistically take on given its available capacity.
concepts.assessment_target: Given team size and velocity history, calculate available capacity for a planning period and reconcile it against roadmap scope.
concepts.practice_objective: Calculate available capacity for a sample team over a quarter and flag over-commitment.
concepts.central_mental_model: Capacity as the hard constraint the roadmap's ambition must be reconciled against.

toc_location.tile_summary: Assign roadmap themes to concrete release windows, then order the underlying features within each release by dependency, value, and risk.

concepts.primary_objective: Sequence roadmap themes into concrete release cycles.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a roadmap, assign roadmap items to specific release windows and justify the ordering.
concepts.practice_objective: Sequence 5 sample roadmap items into 3 release cycles.
concepts.central_mental_model: Release planning as slicing the roadmap's sequencing into shippable cycles, one level more granular than the roadmap itself.

toc_location.tile_summary: Assign roadmap themes to concrete release windows, then order the underlying features within each release by dependency, value, and risk.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Already ranked in relative importance/value order by some prioritization method -- the specific method isn't required here, only that a ranking already exists to sequence against.

concepts.primary_objective: Order features/work within a plan based on dependency, value, and risk.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of features with dependencies, produce a valid sequence and justify the ordering.
concepts.practice_objective: Sequence 4 sample features given their dependencies and relative value.
concepts.central_mental_model: Sequencing as satisfying a dependency graph while maximizing early value delivery.

toc_location.tile_summary: Estimate delivery as a probabilistic date range tied to stated assumptions, then translate roadmap themes and capacity into a bounded, committed quarterly plan.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A team's historical average throughput per sprint, used as the basis for converting a scope of work into a calendar date range.
A fixed time-boxed iteration used to plan and estimate near-term delivery work.

concepts.primary_objective: Estimate calendar delivery dates for roadmap items given team capacity and scope.
concepts.assessment_target: Given scope and team velocity, estimate a delivery date range and state the confidence/assumptions behind it.
concepts.practice_objective: Produce a date range estimate for a sample initiative given provided velocity data.
concepts.central_mental_model: Timeline estimates as probabilistic ranges tied to assumptions, not single-point promises.

toc_location.tile_summary: Estimate delivery as a probabilistic date range tied to stated assumptions, then translate roadmap themes and capacity into a bounded, committed quarterly plan.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Already ranked in relative importance/value order by some prioritization method -- the specific method isn't required here, only that a ranking already exists to sequence against.

concepts.primary_objective: Set a coherent set of priorities and goals for a single quarter that ladder up to the roadmap.
concepts.assessment_target: Given roadmap themes and capacity, produce a quarterly plan with prioritized goals.
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a quarterly plan (3-5 priorities) for a sample team given roadmap themes and capacity.
concepts.central_mental_model: The quarter as the planning unit that translates roadmap direction into a committed, bounded slice of work.

toc_location.tile_summary: Scope a multi-sprint initiative with a clear goal and success criteria, then identify and resolve the cross-team dependencies that could block its roadmap-level sequencing.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A fixed-length iteration (commonly 1-2 weeks) used in agile delivery frameworks such as Scrum, during which a team completes a defined slice of work -- introduced formally later in agile_delivery, but used here to describe an initiative as 'multi-sprint' work.
A high-level grouping label used to cluster related initiatives on a roadmap.

concepts.primary_objective: Scope a multi-sprint initiative (a program-level body of work) with a clear goal and success criteria.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a strategic theme, define an initiative's scope, goal, and success criteria.
concepts.practice_objective: Write an initiative brief (goal, scope, success criteria) for a sample strategic theme.
concepts.central_mental_model: An initiative as the mid-altitude unit between a roadmap theme and individual backlog items.

toc_location.tile_summary: Scope a multi-sprint initiative with a clear goal and success criteria, then identify and resolve the cross-team dependencies that could block its roadmap-level sequencing.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A fixed-length iteration (commonly 1-2 weeks) used in agile delivery frameworks such as Scrum, during which a team completes a defined slice of work -- introduced formally later in agile_delivery, but used here to describe the cross-team dependency's own delivery timeframe.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify and manage cross-team dependencies that affect roadmap-level sequencing.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a roadmap with cross-team dependencies, identify blocking dependencies and propose a sequencing fix.
concepts.practice_objective: Map dependencies for a sample multi-team roadmap and reorder items to resolve one blocking dependency.
concepts.central_mental_model: Roadmap dependencies as sequencing constraints between teams, distinct from day-to-day sprint-level blockers.

toc_location.tile_summary: Descope a feature idea to the minimum that tests its riskiest assumption, then plot a set of initiatives on a value-versus-effort 2x2 to spot quick wins.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A testable belief about what will create value, framed so an experiment can prove or disprove it.

concepts.primary_objective: Define the minimum set of functionality needed to test a product hypothesis with real users.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a feature idea, cut it down to an MVP scope and justify what was excluded.
concepts.practice_objective: Descope a sample feature idea to its MVP and list 3 things deliberately cut.
concepts.central_mental_model: MVP as the smallest experiment that tests the riskiest assumption, not a smaller version of the full product.

toc_location.tile_summary: Descope a feature idea to the minimum that tests its riskiest assumption, then plot a set of initiatives on a value-versus-effort 2x2 to spot quick wins.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The estimated cost/complexity of building an item (development time, engineering effort), used as one input into a prioritization score -- distinct from the size units taught in effort_estimation, since here it's a rough directional input rather than a formal points estimate.

concepts.primary_objective: Plot initiatives on a value-vs-effort 2x2 to identify quick wins and time sinks.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of initiatives with value/effort estimates, place them correctly on a 2x2 and identify the quick wins.
concepts.practice_objective: Plot 6 sample initiatives on a value-effort matrix and name the quick wins.
concepts.central_mental_model: The 2x2 as a fast visual triage tool, not a precise scoring method.

toc_location.tile_title: Impact Assessment, RICE, ICE & Weighted Scoring
toc_location.tile_summary: Estimate and justify an initiative's likely impact, score it with RICE's reach/impact/confidence/effort composite, apply ICE for a faster low-data version, and build a custom weighted-scoring model when neither off-the-shelf framework fits the criteria that matter.

concepts.primary_objective: Judge the likely magnitude of effect an initiative will have on a target outcome before committing resources.
concepts.assessment_target: Given an initiative and a target metric, estimate and justify its likely impact.
concepts.practice_objective: Estimate the likely impact of a sample initiative on a given metric and state the confidence level.
concepts.central_mental_model: Impact assessment as the standalone estimation skill that feeds the impact inputs used by RICE/ICE/Kano, rather than a framework of its own.

toc_location.tile_title: Impact Assessment, RICE, ICE & Weighted Scoring
toc_location.tile_summary: Estimate and justify an initiative's likely impact, score it with RICE's reach/impact/confidence/effort composite, apply ICE for a faster low-data version, and build a custom weighted-scoring model when neither off-the-shelf framework fits the criteria that matter.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The estimated cost/complexity of building an item (development time, engineering effort), used as one input into a prioritization score -- distinct from the size units taught in effort_estimation, since here it's a rough directional input rather than a formal points estimate.

concepts.primary_objective: Score and rank initiatives using Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort.
concepts.assessment_target: Given initiative data, calculate RICE scores and rank the initiatives.
concepts.practice_objective: Score 4 sample initiatives using RICE and rank them.
concepts.central_mental_model: RICE as a single composite score balancing reach/impact/confidence against effort cost.

toc_location.tile_title: Impact Assessment, RICE, ICE & Weighted Scoring
toc_location.tile_summary: Estimate and justify an initiative's likely impact, score it with RICE's reach/impact/confidence/effort composite, apply ICE for a faster low-data version, and build a custom weighted-scoring model when neither off-the-shelf framework fits the criteria that matter.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The estimated cost/complexity of building an item (development time, engineering effort), used as one input into a prioritization score -- distinct from the size units taught in effort_estimation, since here it's a rough directional input rather than a formal points estimate.

concepts.primary_objective: Score and rank initiatives using Impact, Confidence, and Ease for fast, low-data prioritization.
concepts.assessment_target: Given initiative descriptions, assign ICE scores and rank them.
concepts.practice_objective: Score 4 sample initiatives using ICE and rank them.
concepts.central_mental_model: ICE as a lightweight, effort-cheap alternative to RICE for quick directional prioritization.

toc_location.tile_title: Impact Assessment, RICE, ICE & Weighted Scoring
toc_location.tile_summary: Estimate and justify an initiative's likely impact, score it with RICE's reach/impact/confidence/effort composite, apply ICE for a faster low-data version, and build a custom weighted-scoring model when neither off-the-shelf framework fits the criteria that matter.

concepts.primary_objective: Rank initiatives using a custom weighted set of criteria relevant to the product context.
concepts.assessment_target: Given criteria and weights, calculate a weighted score for a set of initiatives and rank them.
concepts.practice_objective: Build a weighted scoring model with 3 criteria and score 3 sample initiatives.
concepts.central_mental_model: Weighted scoring as a customizable prioritization model for when off-the-shelf frameworks like RICE/ICE don't fit the criteria that matter.

toc_location.tile_summary: Two analytical reasoning frameworks for prioritization judgment: explicitly weighing competing priorities against constraints, and classifying features by the shape of customer satisfaction they produce.

concepts.primary_objective: Explicitly weigh competing options against each other when a prioritization framework alone doesn't resolve a decision.
concepts.assessment_target: Given two competing options with pros/cons, articulate the tradeoff and make a reasoned recommendation.
concepts.practice_objective: Write a tradeoff analysis (pros/cons + recommendation) for a sample two-option decision.
concepts.central_mental_model: Tradeoff analysis as the reasoning layer applied when scoring frameworks produce a near-tie or don't capture the real conflict.

toc_location.tile_summary: Two analytical reasoning frameworks for prioritization judgment: explicitly weighing competing priorities against constraints, and classifying features by the shape of customer satisfaction they produce.

concepts.primary_objective: Classify features by the type of customer satisfaction they produce (basic, performance, delighter).
concepts.assessment_target: Given feature/customer-reaction data, classify features into Kano categories and justify roadmap implications.
concepts.practice_objective: Classify 4 sample features into Kano categories given customer reaction descriptions.
concepts.central_mental_model: Kano as mapping features onto a satisfaction curve, distinguishing must-haves from differentiators.

toc_location.tile_summary: Two framing conventions for communicating prioritization decisions outward: a roadmap-communication tiering scheme, and a release-scoping filter for classifying requirements as must/should/could/won't.

concepts.primary_objective: Communicate roadmap priorities using coarse time horizons instead of fixed dates.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of initiatives, bucket them into Now/Next/Later and justify placement.
concepts.practice_objective: Bucket 6 sample initiatives into Now/Next/Later.
concepts.central_mental_model: Now-Next-Later as a confidence-calibrated alternative to date-based roadmaps, hiding false precision the further out an item sits.

toc_location.tile_summary: Two framing conventions for communicating prioritization decisions outward: a roadmap-communication tiering scheme, and a release-scoping filter for classifying requirements as must/should/could/won't.

inline_vocabulary.definition: the full set of not-yet-scheduled work items a team maintains; distinct from a committed release scope.

concepts.primary_objective: Classify requirements by Must/Should/Could/Won't to scope a single release.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a requirements list, classify each into MoSCoW categories and justify what's cut for the current release.
concepts.practice_objective: Classify 6 sample requirements using MoSCoW for a sample release.
concepts.central_mental_model: MoSCoW as a requirements-scoping filter for one release, distinct from ongoing backlog scoring frameworks.

toc_location.tile_summary: Map stakeholders by influence and interest to plan engagement, align other functions' incentives toward a shared outcome, and design a process to reach consensus or a documented disagree-and-commit.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify stakeholders and manage their expectations and influence over a product initiative.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a project, map stakeholders by influence/interest and propose an engagement approach for each.
concepts.practice_objective: Map 4 sample stakeholders on an influence/interest grid and propose one engagement action per stakeholder.
concepts.central_mental_model: Stakeholder management as proactively matching engagement effort to each stakeholder's influence and interest.

toc_location.tile_summary: Map stakeholders by influence and interest to plan engagement, align other functions' incentives toward a shared outcome, and design a process to reach consensus or a documented disagree-and-commit.

concepts.primary_objective: Work effectively with functions outside product (eng, design, sales, support) toward a shared outcome.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a cross-functional conflict scenario, propose a collaboration approach that respects each function's constraints.
concepts.practice_objective: Propose how to resolve a sample cross-functional friction point (e.g., eng vs. sales priorities).
concepts.central_mental_model: Cross-functional collaboration as aligning different functions' incentives toward one shared goal, not just information sharing.

toc_location.tile_summary: Map stakeholders by influence and interest to plan engagement, align other functions' incentives toward a shared outcome, and design a process to reach consensus or a documented disagree-and-commit.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A decision convention where participants who disagreed with a decision still commit to executing it once it's made, rather than the group waiting for unanimous agreement.

concepts.primary_objective: Bring a group with differing opinions to a shared, workable decision.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a scenario with disagreeing stakeholders, propose a process to reach consensus (or documented disagree-and-commit).
concepts.practice_objective: Design a short consensus-building process for a sample 3-way disagreement.
concepts.central_mental_model: Consensus building as engineering agreement (or explicit disagree-and-commit), not unanimous enthusiasm.

toc_location.tile_title: Audience Adaptation, Status Reporting, Executive Comms & Messaging
toc_location.tile_summary: Reframe one message for different audiences without changing the underlying truth, deliver a recurring low-friction status update, lead with the decision or ask when briefing executives, and translate a value proposition into audience-facing product messaging.

concepts.primary_objective: Adapt the content and framing of a message to fit a specific audience's needs and context.
concepts.assessment_target: Given one message and two different audiences, adapt the content/tone appropriately for each.
concepts.practice_objective: Rewrite a sample message for two different audiences (e.g., engineer vs. executive).
concepts.central_mental_model: The same underlying information reframed per audience, not two different truths.

toc_location.tile_title: Audience Adaptation, Status Reporting, Executive Comms & Messaging
toc_location.tile_summary: Reframe one message for different audiences without changing the underlying truth, deliver a recurring low-friction status update, lead with the decision or ask when briefing executives, and translate a value proposition into audience-facing product messaging.

concepts.primary_objective: Communicate initiative progress accurately and concisely to relevant audiences on a regular cadence.
concepts.assessment_target: Given project status data, write a status update covering progress, risks, and next steps.
concepts.practice_objective: Write a status update for a sample in-flight initiative.
concepts.central_mental_model: Status reporting as a recurring, low-friction signal of progress and risk, not a retrospective narrative.

toc_location.tile_title: Audience Adaptation, Status Reporting, Executive Comms & Messaging
toc_location.tile_summary: Reframe one message for different audiences without changing the underlying truth, deliver a recurring low-friction status update, lead with the decision or ask when briefing executives, and translate a value proposition into audience-facing product messaging.

concepts.primary_objective: Communicate to executives/leadership concisely, leading with the decision or ask.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a detailed update, condense it into an executive-ready summary (headline, ask, risk) in a fixed short format.
concepts.practice_objective: Condense a sample detailed project update into a 3-line executive summary.
concepts.central_mental_model: Executive communication as leading with the bottom line and the ask, deferring detail until requested.

toc_location.tile_title: Audience Adaptation, Status Reporting, Executive Comms & Messaging
toc_location.tile_summary: Reframe one message for different audiences without changing the underlying truth, deliver a recurring low-friction status update, lead with the decision or ask when briefing executives, and translate a value proposition into audience-facing product messaging.

concepts.primary_objective: Craft messaging that communicates a product's value in language the target audience understands.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a value proposition and audience, write product messaging (headline + supporting points).
concepts.practice_objective: Write a headline and 2 supporting bullets for a sample product/audience pair.
concepts.central_mental_model: Messaging as translating an internal value proposition into audience-facing language.

toc_location.tile_summary: Frame the same roadmap sequencing differently for an executive, sales, or engineering audience, resolve a stakeholder conflict by naming the tradeoff being made, and negotiate scope or priority by trading on shared goals rather than positional power.

concepts.primary_objective: Present a roadmap to a given audience in a way that sets accurate expectations.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a roadmap and an audience (exec, sales, eng), adapt the framing and level of detail shown.
concepts.practice_objective: Rewrite a sample roadmap slide for two different audiences (executive vs. engineering).
concepts.central_mental_model: Roadmap communication as audience-specific framing of the same underlying sequencing, avoiding false delivery-date certainty.

toc_location.tile_summary: Frame the same roadmap sequencing differently for an executive, sales, or engineering audience, resolve a stakeholder conflict by naming the tradeoff being made, and negotiate scope or priority by trading on shared goals rather than positional power.

concepts.primary_objective: Resolve a disagreement between stakeholders in a way that keeps the initiative moving.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a conflict scenario, propose a resolution approach and articulate the tradeoff being made.
concepts.practice_objective: Propose a resolution for a sample stakeholder conflict and state what tradeoff it accepts.
concepts.central_mental_model: Conflict resolution as making an explicit tradeoff decision, not just smoothing over disagreement.

toc_location.tile_summary: Frame the same roadmap sequencing differently for an executive, sales, or engineering audience, resolve a stakeholder conflict by naming the tradeoff being made, and negotiate scope or priority by trading on shared goals rather than positional power.

concepts.primary_objective: Negotiate priorities or scope with a stakeholder who has different goals, often without formal authority.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a negotiation scenario, propose an approach that finds a workable middle ground.
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a negotiation approach for a sample scope-cut request from an exec.
concepts.central_mental_model: Negotiation as influencing without authority, trading on shared goals rather than positional power.

toc_location.tile_title: Backlog Management, Effort Estimation & Feasibility Conversations
toc_location.tile_summary: Reorganize and reprioritize a backlog as a living reflection of current priority, facilitate relative story-point sizing rather than absolute time prediction, and raise the right feasibility questions with engineering before a feature is committed.

concepts.primary_objective: Own and maintain a prioritized, well-groomed backlog that reflects current priorities.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a messy backlog, reorganize and reprioritize it and justify the new ordering.
concepts.practice_objective: Reprioritize a sample 10-item backlog and justify the top 3.
concepts.central_mental_model: The backlog as a living, ordered list reflecting current priority, not an archive of every idea ever proposed.

toc_location.tile_title: Backlog Management, Effort Estimation & Feasibility Conversations
toc_location.tile_summary: Reorganize and reprioritize a backlog as a living reflection of current priority, facilitate relative story-point sizing rather than absolute time prediction, and raise the right feasibility questions with engineering before a feature is committed.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A fixed time-boxed iteration used to plan and estimate near-term delivery work.

An estimation unit representing relative effort/size/complexity (not literal time), assigned to a work item and compared against a reference story on a scale (commonly a Fibonacci-like sequence), used for sizing rather than absolute-hour prediction.

concepts.primary_objective: Facilitate relative sizing of backlog items so a team can plan sprint capacity.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of stories, produce relative size estimates (story points/t-shirt sizes) and justify outliers.
concepts.practice_objective: Size 4 sample stories relative to each other using story points.
concepts.central_mental_model: Estimation as relative comparison between items, not an absolute time prediction.

toc_location.tile_title: Backlog Management, Effort Estimation & Feasibility Conversations
toc_location.tile_summary: Reorganize and reprioritize a backlog as a living reflection of current priority, facilitate relative story-point sizing rather than absolute time prediction, and raise the right feasibility questions with engineering before a feature is committed.

concepts.primary_objective: Hold a PM-depth conversation with engineering to sanity-check a proposed solution's feasibility before committing it to a roadmap.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a proposed feature, identify the right feasibility questions to raise with engineering and interpret their answers.
concepts.practice_objective: List 3 feasibility questions a PM should ask engineering about a sample feature idea.
concepts.central_mental_model: Feasibility conversation as PM-depth risk-surfacing, not a substitute for an engineer's own technical design.

toc_location.tile_title: Sprint Planning, Daily Standup, Sprint Review & Retrospective
toc_location.tile_summary: Present priority and clarify acceptance criteria to form a sound sprint commitment, listen for blockers and scope risk at the daily standup without turning it into a status meeting, demo completed work and gather stakeholder feedback at Sprint Review, and contribute retro improvement items within a PM/PO's actual ownership.

inline_vocabulary.definition: An agile framework for iterative delivery organized around fixed-length sprints and a defined cycle of ceremonies (planning, daily sync, review, retrospective).
The Scrum role accountable for the product backlog and its priorities -- distinct from a Product Manager (PM), a role this curriculum uses without ever formally distinguishing.

concepts.primary_objective: Understand what a PM/PO contributes to Sprint Planning: presenting priority and clarifying acceptance criteria for candidate backlog items.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a backlog, identify what a PM/PO should present and clarify during sprint planning to enable a sound sprint commitment.
concepts.practice_objective: Prepare a short sprint-planning briefing for a sample backlog slice.
concepts.central_mental_model: Sprint Planning as the ceremony where roadmap priority meets team capacity to form a concrete sprint commitment.

toc_location.tile_title: Sprint Planning, Daily Standup, Sprint Review & Retrospective
toc_location.tile_summary: Present priority and clarify acceptance criteria to form a sound sprint commitment, listen for blockers and scope risk at the daily standup without turning it into a status meeting, demo completed work and gather stakeholder feedback at Sprint Review, and contribute retro improvement items within a PM/PO's actual ownership.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The Scrum framework's formal name for the daily standup ceremony -- a short, time-boxed daily sync, not a status meeting.

concepts.primary_objective: Understand the PM/PO's role in a Daily Scrum: listening for blockers and scope risk without turning it into a status meeting.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a standup transcript, identify blockers a PM/PO should follow up on outside the meeting.
concepts.practice_objective: Review a sample standup transcript and list follow-up actions for the PM/PO.
concepts.central_mental_model: The standup as a synchronization signal for the team, with PM/PO follow-up happening outside the meeting, not during it.

toc_location.tile_title: Sprint Planning, Daily Standup, Sprint Review & Retrospective
toc_location.tile_summary: Present priority and clarify acceptance criteria to form a sound sprint commitment, listen for blockers and scope risk at the daily standup without turning it into a status meeting, demo completed work and gather stakeholder feedback at Sprint Review, and contribute retro improvement items within a PM/PO's actual ownership.

inline_vocabulary.definition: the sum of completed, potentially shippable product work produced during a sprint.

concepts.primary_objective: Understand the PM/PO's role in a Sprint Review: demoing completed work to stakeholders and gathering feedback against the goal.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a sprint's completed work, prepare what a PM/PO should demo and what feedback to solicit.
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a sprint review agenda for a sample completed increment.
concepts.central_mental_model: Sprint Review as the checkpoint where completed work meets real stakeholder feedback before it's called done.

toc_location.tile_title: Sprint Planning, Daily Standup, Sprint Review & Retrospective
toc_location.tile_summary: Present priority and clarify acceptance criteria to form a sound sprint commitment, listen for blockers and scope risk at the daily standup without turning it into a status meeting, demo completed work and gather stakeholder feedback at Sprint Review, and contribute retro improvement items within a PM/PO's actual ownership.

concepts.primary_objective: Understand the PM/PO's role in a Sprint Retrospective: contributing to process improvement without dominating the discussion.
concepts.assessment_target: Given retro notes, identify which improvement items are within a PM/PO's ownership to act on.
concepts.practice_objective: Triage a sample list of retro action items into 'PM/PO owns' vs 'team owns'.
concepts.central_mental_model: The retro as a process-improvement loop distinct from the work-review loop of Sprint Review.

toc_location.tile_title: Backlog Refinement, Tech Debt, Dependency Tracking & Kanban
toc_location.tile_summary: Prepare raw backlog items into sprint-ready shape ahead of formal planning, interleave debt paydown with feature work as a shared capacity tradeoff, flag and mitigate short-horizon cross-team blockers, and diagnose flow bottlenecks against WIP limits on a Kanban board.

concepts.primary_objective: Prepare upcoming backlog items (clarify, size, split) so they're ready for a future sprint.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a raw backlog item, refine it into a sprint-ready item with clear scope.
concepts.practice_objective: Refine one sample vague backlog item into a sprint-ready item.
concepts.central_mental_model: Refinement as ongoing preparation work distinct from the formal, time-boxed Sprint Planning ceremony.

toc_location.tile_title: Backlog Refinement, Tech Debt, Dependency Tracking & Kanban
toc_location.tile_summary: Prepare raw backlog items into sprint-ready shape ahead of formal planning, interleave debt paydown with feature work as a shared capacity tradeoff, flag and mitigate short-horizon cross-team blockers, and diagnose flow bottlenecks against WIP limits on a Kanban board.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The implied future cost of choosing an expedient (rather than the best) engineering solution now -- work deferred that will need to be paid down later, competing with new feature work for the same delivery capacity.
A fixed time-boxed iteration used to plan and estimate near-term delivery work.

concepts.primary_objective: Balance technical debt paydown against feature work in prioritization decisions.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a backlog with debt items and features, decide how to interleave them and justify the ratio.
concepts.practice_objective: Allocate a sample sprint's capacity between 2 debt items and 3 features, and justify the split.
concepts.central_mental_model: Tech debt as a prioritization input competing for the same capacity as feature work, not a separate track to ignore.

toc_location.tile_title: Backlog Refinement, Tech Debt, Dependency Tracking & Kanban
toc_location.tile_summary: Prepare raw backlog items into sprint-ready shape ahead of formal planning, interleave debt paydown with feature work as a shared capacity tradeoff, flag and mitigate short-horizon cross-team blockers, and diagnose flow bottlenecks against WIP limits on a Kanban board.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify and track blocking dependencies between teams at the sprint level.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a sprint backlog with cross-team dependencies, identify blockers and propose a mitigation.
concepts.practice_objective: Flag the blocking dependency in a sample sprint backlog and propose a workaround.
concepts.central_mental_model: Sprint-level dependency tracking as short-horizon blocker management, distinct from roadmap-level dependency planning.

toc_location.tile_title: Backlog Refinement, Tech Debt, Dependency Tracking & Kanban
toc_location.tile_summary: Prepare raw backlog items into sprint-ready shape ahead of formal planning, interleave debt paydown with feature work as a shared capacity tradeoff, flag and mitigate short-horizon cross-team blockers, and diagnose flow bottlenecks against WIP limits on a Kanban board.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Work-in-progress limits -- a cap on how many items are allowed in a given workflow column at once, used to expose and resolve flow bottlenecks.

concepts.primary_objective: Manage a Kanban board's flow and WIP limits to keep work moving smoothly.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a Kanban board state, identify flow bottlenecks and recommend a WIP-limit adjustment.
concepts.practice_objective: Diagnose a sample Kanban board with a stuck column and propose a fix.
concepts.central_mental_model: Kanban as managing continuous flow against WIP limits, distinct from the sprint-based cadence of Scrum ceremonies.

toc_location.tile_summary: Check completed work against a shared Definition of Done distinct from item-specific acceptance criteria, then coordinate the release checklist and risk review that gets it safely into production.

concepts.primary_objective: Define and apply the shared checklist that determines when a piece of work is truly complete.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a completed story, check it against a Definition of Done and identify any gaps.
concepts.practice_objective: Check a sample completed story against a given DoD checklist and flag missing items.
concepts.central_mental_model: DoD as a fixed, team-wide completeness bar applied to every item, distinct from item-specific acceptance criteria.

toc_location.tile_summary: Check completed work against a shared Definition of Done distinct from item-specific acceptance criteria, then coordinate the release checklist and risk review that gets it safely into production.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A fixed time-boxed iteration used to plan and estimate near-term delivery work.

concepts.primary_objective: Coordinate the steps needed to safely ship a set of completed work to production.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of completed items, produce a release checklist and identify launch risks.
concepts.practice_objective: Write a release checklist for a sample set of completed features.
concepts.central_mental_model: Release management as the go/no-go coordination step between 'done in sprint' and 'live for users'.

toc_location.tile_title: North Star Metrics, OKRs & Leading/Lagging Indicators
toc_location.tile_summary: Propose a North Star Metric that stands in for value delivered, write an objective with measurable key results, and classify metrics as early-warning leading signals versus late-arriving lagging outcomes.

concepts.primary_objective: Identify the single metric that best captures the core value a product delivers to customers.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a product's value proposition, propose a North Star Metric and justify why it captures value delivered.
concepts.practice_objective: Propose a North Star Metric for a sample product and justify the choice against 2 alternatives.
concepts.central_mental_model: The North Star Metric as the one metric standing in for customer value creation, around which other metrics organize.

toc_location.tile_title: North Star Metrics, OKRs & Leading/Lagging Indicators
toc_location.tile_summary: Propose a North Star Metric that stands in for value delivered, write an objective with measurable key results, and classify metrics as early-warning leading signals versus late-arriving lagging outcomes.

concepts.primary_objective: Set an ambitious objective paired with measurable key results using the OKR format.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a strategic goal, write an objective with 2-3 measurable key results.
concepts.practice_objective: Write one OKR (objective + 3 key results) for a sample team goal.
concepts.central_mental_model: OKRs as pairing a qualitative aspiration (Objective) with quantitative proof of achieving it (Key Results).

toc_location.tile_title: North Star Metrics, OKRs & Leading/Lagging Indicators
toc_location.tile_summary: Propose a North Star Metric that stands in for value delivered, write an objective with measurable key results, and classify metrics as early-warning leading signals versus late-arriving lagging outcomes.

concepts.primary_objective: Distinguish leading indicators (predictive, early) from lagging indicators (outcome, late) when choosing what to monitor.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of metrics, classify each as leading or lagging and justify which to monitor for early warning.
concepts.practice_objective: Classify 4 sample metrics as leading or lagging.
concepts.central_mental_model: Leading indicators as early-warning signals; lagging indicators as confirmed outcomes measured too late to act on directly.

toc_location.tile_title: Hypothesis Testing, Dashboard Interpretation & Tracking Plans
toc_location.tile_summary: Rewrite a product assumption as a falsifiable, testable hypothesis, interpret a dashboard's trends and anomalies without over-reading correlation as causation, and write a tracking plan that guarantees the data needed to measure success will actually exist.

concepts.primary_objective: Formulate and validate a falsifiable hypothesis before running an experiment.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a product assumption, rewrite it as a falsifiable hypothesis with a clear pass/fail condition.
concepts.practice_objective: Convert two vague product assumptions into falsifiable, testable hypotheses.
concepts.central_mental_model: A hypothesis as a falsifiable claim that an experiment is designed to accept or reject, at PM-appropriate depth rather than formal statistical inference.

toc_location.tile_title: Hypothesis Testing, Dashboard Interpretation & Tracking Plans
toc_location.tile_summary: Rewrite a product assumption as a falsifiable, testable hypothesis, interpret a dashboard's trends and anomalies without over-reading correlation as causation, and write a tracking plan that guarantees the data needed to measure success will actually exist.

concepts.primary_objective: Read a product analytics dashboard and draw correct conclusions from it.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a dashboard, identify a notable trend/anomaly and propose a plausible explanation to investigate.
concepts.practice_objective: Interpret a sample dashboard screenshot and flag one anomaly worth investigating.
concepts.central_mental_model: Dashboard interpretation as pattern-reading plus healthy skepticism about correlation vs. causation.

toc_location.tile_title: Hypothesis Testing, Dashboard Interpretation & Tracking Plans
toc_location.tile_summary: Rewrite a product assumption as a falsifiable, testable hypothesis, interpret a dashboard's trends and anomalies without over-reading correlation as causation, and write a tracking plan that guarantees the data needed to measure success will actually exist.

inline_vocabulary.definition: An event is a discrete user or system action recorded for analytics (e.g. 'signup_completed'); a property is a piece of metadata attached to an event (e.g. 'plan_type'). A tracking plan is the document that defines which events and properties get instrumented.

concepts.primary_objective: Define what events and properties need to be tracked to measure a feature's success before it ships.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a feature and its success metrics, specify the events/properties that must be instrumented to measure them.
concepts.practice_objective: Write a tracking plan (events + properties) for a sample feature's defined success metrics.
concepts.central_mental_model: A tracking plan as a pre-launch measurement contract ensuring the data needed to prove success will actually exist.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify the largest leak in a step-by-step conversion funnel, then read a cohort retention table to isolate which time-anchored group behaves differently and why.

concepts.primary_objective: Analyze a multi-step conversion funnel to find where users drop off.
concepts.assessment_target: Given funnel step data, identify the largest drop-off point and propose a hypothesis for it.
concepts.practice_objective: Analyze a sample funnel's step-by-step conversion rates and identify the biggest leak.
concepts.central_mental_model: The funnel as a sequence of conversion gates, each with its own drop-off rate to diagnose independently.

toc_location.tile_summary: Identify the largest leak in a step-by-step conversion funnel, then read a cohort retention table to isolate which time-anchored group behaves differently and why.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The percentage of a specific cohort (users who started in the same period) still active N periods later -- the core metric cohort analysis tracks, as distinct from a single blended average across all users.
A single average computed across all users regardless of when they joined -- the naive baseline that cohort analysis is contrasted against, because it can mask retention differences between cohorts.

concepts.primary_objective: Compare groups of users by shared start date/attribute to understand retention over time.
concepts.assessment_target: Given cohort retention data, identify which cohort behaves differently and propose why.
concepts.practice_objective: Read a sample cohort retention table and identify the best/worst performing cohort.
concepts.central_mental_model: Cohorts as time-anchored groups that isolate whether a change genuinely shifted behavior, versus a single blended average.

toc_location.tile_title: A/B Testing, Data-Driven Decisions, Feature Flags & Holdouts
toc_location.tile_summary: Design an A/B test's hypothesis, metric, and variants to isolate a causal effect, make and justify a recommendation while naming what the data can't answer, stage a rollout behind feature flags with a rollback trigger, and keep a holdout group to measure true incremental lift.

inline_vocabulary.definition: Sample size is the number of users/observations included in a test; statistical power is the probability the test correctly detects a real effect if one exists. Both determine how long an A/B test must run before its result can be trusted.

concepts.primary_objective: Design and interpret an A/B test to measure the causal effect of a single change.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a proposed change, define a testable hypothesis, primary metric, and sample-size/duration for an A/B test.
concepts.practice_objective: Design an A/B test plan (hypothesis, metric, variants) for a sample feature change.
concepts.central_mental_model: A/B testing as isolating one variable's causal effect via randomized comparison, at PM-appropriate depth rather than full statistical modeling.

toc_location.tile_title: A/B Testing, Data-Driven Decisions, Feature Flags & Holdouts
toc_location.tile_summary: Design an A/B test's hypothesis, metric, and variants to isolate a causal effect, make and justify a recommendation while naming what the data can't answer, stage a rollout behind feature flags with a rollback trigger, and keep a holdout group to measure true incremental lift.

concepts.primary_objective: Use data as a primary input to a product decision, while recognizing its limits.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a decision scenario with available data and its gaps, make and justify a recommendation, naming what the data does not tell you.
concepts.practice_objective: Make a recommendation for a sample decision using provided data, and name one thing the data can't answer.
concepts.central_mental_model: Data as one weighted input to a decision alongside judgment and qualitative context, not an automatic verdict.

toc_location.tile_title: A/B Testing, Data-Driven Decisions, Feature Flags & Holdouts
toc_location.tile_summary: Design an A/B test's hypothesis, metric, and variants to isolate a causal effect, make and justify a recommendation while naming what the data can't answer, stage a rollout behind feature flags with a rollback trigger, and keep a holdout group to measure true incremental lift.

inline_vocabulary.definition: a configuration toggle checked while the application is running, used to turn a feature on or off without a new deployment.
the act of releasing new code to a live environment, distinct from separately toggling that code on for users.
reverting a feature or change back to its prior state, typically by toggling it off rather than redeploying code.

concepts.primary_objective: Use feature flags to control a staged rollout of a change to a subset of users.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a launch plan, define a flag-based rollout sequence (e.g., 1% -> 10% -> 100%) with rollback criteria.
concepts.practice_objective: Write a staged rollout plan with flag percentages and a rollback trigger for a sample feature.
concepts.central_mental_model: A feature flag as a runtime switch that decouples code deployment from user-facing release.

toc_location.tile_title: A/B Testing, Data-Driven Decisions, Feature Flags & Holdouts
toc_location.tile_summary: Design an A/B test's hypothesis, metric, and variants to isolate a causal effect, make and justify a recommendation while naming what the data can't answer, stage a rollout behind feature flags with a rollback trigger, and keep a holdout group to measure true incremental lift.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The portion of an observed outcome (e.g. conversion, revenue) attributable to the change itself, isolated by comparing the treatment group against the holdout/control group's baseline.

concepts.primary_objective: Maintain a holdout group to isolate and measure the long-run incremental impact of a change.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a rollout, define a holdout group size and the metric comparison used to measure incremental lift.
concepts.practice_objective: Specify a holdout group design for a sample feature launch and the comparison metric.
concepts.central_mental_model: A holdout group as a permanent control slice that keeps a true baseline available even after full rollout.

toc_location.tile_summary: Check a launch against readiness gates (support, sales, monitoring), sequence internal/external communications against launch day, and prepare an enablement packet for support and sales.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A binary launch decision (proceed or hold) reached by evaluating a set of readiness-gate items together; expressed with a justification for any item that is not ready ('red').

concepts.primary_objective: Assess whether a product or feature is ready to launch by checking it against defined readiness dimensions -- support, sales, and monitoring -- before it ships to customers.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a launch scenario and a set of readiness dimensions, complete a launch readiness checklist and produce a go/no-go recommendation with justification for any red items.
concepts.practice_objective: Fill out a launch readiness checklist for a sample feature launch, identify any items that block go/no-go, and state why.
concepts.central_mental_model: Launch readiness as a cross-functional checklist of deployment gates (support, sales, monitoring) assessed together, not a unilateral engineering-ready decision.

toc_location.tile_summary: Check a launch against readiness gates (support, sales, monitoring), sequence internal/external communications against launch day, and prepare an enablement packet for support and sales.

inline_vocabulary.definition: The bounded period, timed relative to launch day (before / at / after), during which a specific message is appropriate to send to a given audience.

concepts.primary_objective: Plan the timing, sequencing, and audience segmentation of internal and external launch communications for a product or feature launch.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a launch date and a list of internal/external stakeholders, produce a communication plan specifying what message goes to which audience and when relative to launch day.
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a launch communication timeline for a sample feature that names at least three distinct audiences and the messaging window for each.
concepts.central_mental_model: Launch communication as a sequenced set of audience-specific messages timed against launch day, not a single simultaneous announcement.

toc_location.tile_summary: Check a launch against readiness gates (support, sales, monitoring), sequence internal/external communications against launch day, and prepare an enablement packet for support and sales.

inline_vocabulary.definition: A bundled reference (FAQ, talking points, known limitations) that equips a support or sales rep to represent a feature to customers unaided, distinct from external marketing collateral.

concepts.primary_objective: Prepare sales and support teams with the materials and talking points they need to represent a new feature or product to customers without engineering hand-holding.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a feature launch, produce a basic enablement packet (FAQ, talking points, known limitations) that a support or sales rep can use unaided.
concepts.practice_objective: Write an FAQ and talking-points one-pager for a sample feature aimed at a support team fielding customer questions.
concepts.central_mental_model: Enablement as translating internal feature knowledge into a support/sales-ready reference, distinct from external marketing collateral.

toc_location.tile_summary: Draft a collaboration plan with clear checkpoints and decision lanes for a design engagement, then build a stage-by-stage journey map that surfaces the user's top friction point.

concepts.primary_objective: Partner effectively with designers throughout the product development process, from ideation to handoff.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a design review scenario, identify the PM's contribution vs. the designer's decision authority.
concepts.practice_objective: Draft a collaboration plan (checkpoints, inputs needed) for a sample design engagement.
concepts.central_mental_model: Design collaboration as a partnership with clear lanes: PM owns problem/priority, designer owns solution/craft.

toc_location.tile_summary: Draft a collaboration plan with clear checkpoints and decision lanes for a design engagement, then build a stage-by-stage journey map that surfaces the user's top friction point.

concepts.primary_objective: Map a user's end-to-end journey through a product to identify friction points and opportunities.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a user scenario, construct a journey map with stages, actions, and pain points.
concepts.practice_objective: Build a journey map for a sample user flow and mark the top friction point.
concepts.central_mental_model: A journey map as the user's experience laid out stage-by-stage, surfacing friction invisible in a single screen or flow.

toc_location.tile_summary: Rewrite taste-based critique as objective-anchored feedback tied to user goals, then synthesize a set of usability test findings into a ranked list of design changes.

concepts.primary_objective: Give actionable, objective-anchored feedback on wireframes and prototypes.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a wireframe/prototype, write feedback that ties back to user goals and success metrics rather than personal taste.
concepts.practice_objective: Critique a sample wireframe and rewrite two taste-based comments as objective-anchored feedback.
concepts.central_mental_model: Design feedback anchored to user goals and success criteria, not personal aesthetic preference.

concepts.concept_name: User Testing Synthesis (Findings to Design Decisions)

toc_location.tile_summary: Rewrite taste-based critique as objective-anchored feedback tied to user goals, then synthesize a set of usability test findings into a ranked list of design changes.

concepts.primary_objective: Translate usability test findings into concrete design decisions.
concepts.assessment_target: Given a set of usability test findings, prioritize them and recommend specific design changes.
concepts.practice_objective: Synthesize a sample set of test findings into a ranked list of design changes.
concepts.central_mental_model: Test synthesis as the bridge that converts raw observed behavior into a prioritized set of design changes.
